base.prompt: Create ONE finished, production-quality 2D game character asset, on a truly TRANSPARENT background, not a concept sheet. Subject: the BASE PLAYER FISH for the existing EVO game. Use the attached reference fish as the exact art-direction anchor: a charming but prehistoric stout slate-blue silver fish, softly brushed painterly modelling, very dark navy organically inked silhouette, ivory grey fin membranes, large readable cream-and-black circular eye, silver-white belly and simple dark gill fold. Match its specific character identity and handmade game style closely, not photorealistic, not generic vector art. Strict orthographic SIDE VIEW, head facing RIGHT, perfectly horizontal, relaxed neutral swimming pose, entire tail and every fin included. Mouth shut except a tiny dark lip line and two or three small existing teeth; ordinary small jaw, no enlarged fangs. BASE FORM with no external bone armour: smooth modest rounded forehead, small compact snout, integrated cheek/gill volumes, friendly alert eye. It must look like a purposeful and exceptionally well-designed playable character, recognisable at very small sprite sizes; confident outline, elegant limited-value shading, restrained texture, subtle painterly highlights. Same proportions as reference: tail occupies left 22%, body middle 48%, head right 30%. Keep generous transparent breathing room around all extremities. No background of any colour, no shadows outside the character, no ground, no halo, no water, no particles, no frames, no text, no watermark. Landscape canvas, high-resolution clean alpha PNG suitable as an unanimated master asset; use almost the full canvas with approximately 8% empty padding. This is the base of a four-stage skull-evolution series, so retain a stable silhouette, fins, eye design and colour palette for the later stages. Do not draw extra fish, extra angles or detached components.

variants.prompt:
Create ONE finished, high-quality transparent PNG game character asset, not a concept sheet. EDIT the first reference, the EVO base player fish, to design one discrete SKULL evolution. Keep its hand-painted slate-blue/silver body, pale ivory-grey fins, rounded readable eye, dark organic ink outline, silver-white belly, simple gill fold, tail, dorsal fin and fin arrangement. Same fish identity and roughly the same overall length and full-body proportions, same horizontal orthographic RIGHT-FACING side view and neutral relaxed closed-mouth swimming pose, same top-left soft illumination. Use the second reference ONLY for the material language of natural ivory/grey prehistoric dermal skull plates, not as an excuse to copy its exact armour geometry. Strength must come from a designed skull and ramming silhouette, not scaling the whole fish up. Mouth and bite strength remain BASE level: small integrated lower jaw, two or three tiny teeth only, no large fangs, no elongated predator jaw. Every silhouette must be easy to identify at 90 pixels. Draw coherent interlocking broad bone forms with well-considered anatomy, a sculpted integrated brow and cheek, restrained seams and beautiful painterly modelling. Do not add busy scales, decorative spikes or fantasy armour straps. TRULY TRANSPARENT alpha background; no colour backdrop, no halo, no cast shadow outside the body, no water, no floating particles, no text or numbers, no watermark. Entire tail and all fins fully visible, generous empty margin. Only ONE fish, no comparisons or other viewpoints. Landscape high-resolution canvas matching the base reference framing, ideally 1675 by 939.

STAGE 1, SKULL GREATER THAN 20: the first decisive evolutionary breakthrough. A clearly new but modest low-profile bony forehead cap now strengthens the front of the head. Two or three broad organic mineral-grey ivory plates form a forward-sloping brow and a short solid nose cap, with a small upper cheek plate tucked naturally behind the eye. Preserve much visible slate-blue skin on the lower cheek and most of the head. The forehead becomes slightly wider and firmer, a compact ramming wedge with subtle curved ridge, but no full head helmet or body armour. Distinct from the smooth base, still agile-looking and recognisably the starting fish.
